title: Simulation by testing a subprotocol
statement: Let $s$, $p$, $q_{\mathrm{in}}$, and $q_{\mathrm{out}}$ be deterministic two-party protocols with inputs in $X$ and $Y$ and outputs in $\alpha$. Suppose $s$ is a subprotocol of $p$, with $\mathrm{numLeaves}(s)<\mathrm{numLeaves}(p)$; suppose also that $q_{\mathrm{in}}$ has the same execution function as $s$, and $q_{\mathrm{out}}$ has the same execution function as the protocol obtained by pruning $s$ from $p$. Then the protocol that has Alice test whether her input reaches $s$, has Bob test whether his input reaches $s$, and runs $q_{\mathrm{in}}$ if both tests succeed and $q_{\mathrm{out}}$ otherwise has the same execution function as $p$.
hypotheses_covered: Protocols $s,p,q_{\mathrm{in}},q_{\mathrm{out}}$ with inputs in $X,Y$ and outputs in $\alpha$
$q_{\mathrm{out}}$ and the protocol obtained by pruning $s$ from $p$ have equal execution functions
replaced:
Let $s, p, q_{\mathrm{in}}, q_{\mathrm{out}}$ be deterministic two-party protocols over
input types $X$ and $Y$ with outputs in $\alpha$, where $s$ is a subprotocol of $p$ with
strictly fewer leaves than $p$. Suppose $q_{\mathrm{in}}$ computes the same function as
$s$, and $q_{\mathrm{out}}$ computes the same function as the protocol obtained from $p$
by pruning $s$ away. Then the glued protocol
\texttt{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.testSubprotocol}, which first
tests whether the inputs reach $s$ and then runs $q_{\mathrm{in}}$ or $q_{\mathrm{out}}$
accordingly, computes the same function as $p$ on every pair of inputs $(x,y)$.
